transcript.text: panasonic nn h98 not heating anymore, any fix?

Possibly, but if it runs normally and simply no longer heats, the repair is usually in the microwave’s high-voltage heating system. That is not a safe DIY area: dangerous stored voltage can remain even when it is unplugged, so do not remove the casing or attempt to test internal parts. First rule out the simple causes:
1. Use a microwave-safe cup with water, select normal microwave cooking (not grill, combination, defrost or low power) and full power, then run it for one minute. If the water is hot, it was a setting/mode issue. If it is still cold, there is a genuine heating fault.
2. Check that the door closes firmly and latches cleanly, with no debris around the latch. If it will not start, stops when the door is touched, or behaves as if the door is open, the door interlock is more likely than the heating circuit. If it runs, the timer counts down and the turntable/light operate but the water stays cold, arrange a microwave engineer or consider replacement depending on its age and repair quote. The likely internal causes include the inverter/high-voltage module or magnetron, but the exact failed part cannot be safely identified from outside. With a microwave-safe cup of water, does it run for one minute on full microwave power and leave the water cold, or does it fail to start/cut out? Also, is there an unusually loud heavy buzz?
tried water, stops after about 10-15 seconds with H98 and the water is still cold. door closes fine. no loud buzz, no smell

H98 on a Panasonic, together with stopping after 10–15 seconds and no heat, points to a fault in the microwave high-voltage heating system rather than overheating or a simple setting issue. The leading suspects are the inverter/high-voltage power module, then the magnetron or its feedback circuit. Do not keep running test cycles, and do not remove the casing: hazardous voltage can remain stored inside even unplugged. This needs a microwave engineer to test safely; the external symptoms cannot prove which of those internal parts has failed. The door is less likely because it closes properly and the fault appears consistently after a short run, rather than when the door is moved. Whether repair is worthwhile will depend mainly on the full model and the engineer’s quote, as inverter or magnetron repairs can be relatively costly.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
